name: Bio-inspired / spiking motion branches for identity in MOT (SpikeMOT 2023/IEEE Access 2025; SMTrack 2025; SpikingMOT 2026; event-based MOT with motion features)
bibliography: (1) SpikeMOT: Song Wang*, Zhu Wang*, Can Li, Xiaojuan Qi, Hayden Kwok-Hay So (The University of Hong Kong). 'SpikeMOT: Event-based Multi-Object Tracking with Sparse Motion Features'. arXiv:2309.16987 v1 (29 Sep 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16987 ; journal version IEEE Access, vol. 13, pp. 214-230, 2025 (citation as given in the reference list of SpikingMOT; HKU repository record https://hub.hku.hk/handle/10722/355847 not opened) - preprint and journal are DUPLICATES of one work; journal text not read, numbers below are from arXiv v1. No code link found in the arXiv text. (2) SMTrack: Pengzhi Zhong, Xinzhe Wang, Dan Zeng, Qihua Zhou, Feixiang He, Shuiwang Li. 'SMTrack: End-to-End Trained Spiking Neural Networks for Multi-Object Tracking in RGB Videos'. arXiv:2508.14607 v1 (20 Aug 2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14607 ; journal version IEEE Internet of Things Journal 13(9):18797-18806, 2026 (per the SpikingMOT reference list) [uncertain: journal version not opened]. No code link in the HTML read. (3) SpikingMOT: Yiding Sun, Xiangyang Yang, Dongxu Zhang, Qirui Wang, Zijie Xu, Wenxuan Liu, Shuiwang Li, Jihua Zhu, Zhaofei Yu, Tiejun Huang (Xi'an Jiaotong Univ., Peking Univ., Guilin Univ. of Technology). 'SpikingMOT: A Spike-Driven Multi-Object Tracker'. arXiv:2607.19875 v1 (22 Jul 2026, cs.NE), https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19875 ; preprint, no venue; no code link in the main text. Shares author Shuiwang Li with SMTrack and reuses SMTrack as a baseline - NOT independent of (2). (4) FEMOT/FEMOTR (RGB+event MOT, added as the nearest 'appearance base + event-motion branch' MOT ablation): Shiao Wang, Xiao Wang, Chao Wang, Yitao Li, Menghao Liu, Bo Jiang, Yaowei Wang, Yonghong Tian, Jin Tang. 'FEMOT: Multi-Object Tracking using Frame and Event Cameras'. arXiv:2606.14094 v1 (12 Jun 2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14094 ; code/dataset stated at https://github.com/Event-AHU/FEMOT (not opened). (5) CSAM (RGB-event single-object tracking with MOT-style candidate matching; nearest case of an event-motion embedding added over a frozen strong appearance tracker): Tianlu Zhang, Kurt Debattista, Qiang Zhang, Guiguang Ding, Jungong Han. 'Revisiting Motion Information for RGB-Event Tracking with MOT Philosophy'. NeurIPS 2024, https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/a29f0fc2127c9d8cb1c9d86e423241af-Abstract.html , DOI 10.52202/079017-2836, OpenReview https://openreview.net/forum?id=bzGAELYOyL ; code not listed. Note: no work was found that uses an insect/connectome-constrained motion model (FlyVis-like T4/T5) for MOT identity association; a general search for 'bio-inspired insect motion features + ReID fusion ablation' returned only insect-video trackers with hand-crafted motion features (UNC Charlotte dissertation, not opened).

inputs_state_output: SpikeMOT (event camera only): base = YOLOv5 detector on 2-channel event frames (every 50 ms) + Hungarian matching on Hausdorff distance between detector boxes and tracker positions; added/primary branch = Siamese SNN position estimator (2 CNN blocks + 3 conv+SRM spiking blocks, Tab. 1) taking a template event voxel [2,127,127,100] of each tracked instance and a search voxel [2,255,255,100] around its last position, updated every 10 ms; its score map predicts the target centre; output = new position used to validate/dismiss the Hungarian matches. State = SRM membrane/refractory kernels (tau_s 10 ms, tau_r 1 ms) + template. There is no separate appearance (ReID) branch: the event voxel is simultaneously 'appearance' and 'motion'; identity is maintained by local search (single-object-tracker style) plus position matching. SMTrack (RGB): spiking detector SpikeYOLOX (I-LIF neurons) + training-free TrackTrack association (NSA Kalman, IoU and TrackTrack's appearance feature extractor 'configured identically to TrackTrack'); the spiking part is ONLY the detector - no spiking motion branch is used for identity. SpikingMOT (RGB): replaces the dense motion predictor of MambaTrack by a spiking motion predictor: input = last H=5 normalised box deltas of a track; encoder -> K=8 learnable motion bases each proposing a displacement; LIF spike gates select bases; prediction-error calibration uses the residual between predicted box and matched detection to update the basis posterior carried to the next frame (per-tracklet recurrent state, membrane states initialised per tracklet); output = predicted box for IoU/Hungarian association 'following MambaTrack'. No appearance branch at all. FEMOTR (RGB+event): base = MeMOTR (DAB-Deformable DETR, track queries with EMA long-term memory) on RGB; added branch = event image (accumulated ON/OFF polarities) through the SAME shared ResNet-50; fusion point = Frequency Aware Fusion per scale before the transformer encoder; output = detections and track-query identities. CSAM (RGB-event SOT): base = frozen CEUTrack appearance tracker (ViT, RGB+event voxel jointly) proposing N candidates; per candidate appearance embedding a = conv(PrRoIAlign RGB features) + MLP(score) and motion embedding m = MFE(event features of the candidate) + MLP(box coordinates); spatial-temporal transformer over T=15 frames of candidate tracklets; dual-branch decoder (spatial-temporal decoder + motion decoder) outputs an N x M affinity matrix, Hungarian, threshold 0.75; target re-selected among candidates. Ours: strong base = frozen MASA-R50 RoIAlign appearance per real detection region vs exemplar/previous target/bank; added branch = FlyVis activity (34 output types incl. T4/T5 + 6-neighbour means) from a bounded grey eye crop with temporal state over exemplar+search frames; fusion = concatenation into gradient boosting for 'this region is our target', then full-box transfer gate before ByteTrack. Closest structural analogue: CSAM (frozen strong appearance + per-candidate event-motion embedding + learned matching among distractor candidates). SpikeMOT is closest to our 'eye' (template/search crops with a recurrent spiking state) but its spiking branch IS the appearance model, not an addition to one.
fusion_and_training: SpikeMOT: no fusion with a separate appearance model; Siamese SNN trained from scratch (AdamW, lr 1e-3 -> 1e-4, 50 epochs, batch 4, surrogate gradient), detector trained separately (YOLOv5, COCO init, 100 epochs); the Hungarian matcher is rule-based with SNN validation 'reducing the dependence on the Siamese position estimator'. SMTrack: detector trained end-to-end with Asa-NWD loss; association training-free. SpikingMOT: motion predictor trained alone with box loss (GIoU/L1-type) on current and calibrated next-step prediction (alpha=1.0), spike sparsity regulariser (beta=1e-3) and basis-diversity regulariser (mu=1e-2); detector and motion predictor trained separately; association hyper-parameters copied from MambaTrack/TrackSSM; no appearance fusion. FEMOTR: everything trained jointly (no frozen parts stated), 13 epochs, shared backbone for RGB and event; fusion with residual connections inside FAF. CSAM: TWO-STAGE - appearance tracker trained first and FROZEN while training the candidate matching network (Adam, 15 epochs, lr 4e-5); appearance and motion embeddings are ADDED (a = fe + ce; m = ee + pe) and processed jointly by attention; no zero-init or alpha; the base is protected only by freezing and by the matching threshold (tau_th=0.75) and score threshold (zeta=0.25). None of the five sources uses residual alpha, zero-init, cue masking or any explicit device against modality imbalance; none tests whether the added branch is ignored.
labels_and_loss: SpikeMOT: template-search pairs; 50% positive (same object) and 50% negative, of which 25% same-category different object (explicit hard negatives 'to discriminate semantic distractors based on their motion characteristics'), 12.5% different category, 12.5% object vs background; per-position logistic loss on a score map with radius-R positive disk, balanced weights inside/outside R (Eqs. 4-7). SMTrack: detection losses + Asa-NWD box loss; no identity label. SpikingMOT: box-regression only (identity correspondence used only to form GT trajectories); no identity contrast, no hard negatives. FEMOTR: focal + L1 + GIoU with Hungarian matching of track/detection queries (identity enters via query propagation). CSAM: partially supervised + self-supervised loss on the affinity matrix (L_total = L_self + L_sup, -log A_ij over cycle/assignment pairs) with candidates = target plus distractors proposed by the appearance model, i.e. hard negatives are the appearance-confusable candidates by construction [uncertain: exact supervised loss form in appendix B.2 only partly read]. Class imbalance: SpikeMOT balances positive/negative pairs 1:1; others do not discuss it.
data_camera_resolution_rate: SpikeMOT: DSEC-MOT (built by the authors on DSEC driving recordings, Switzerland): 12 sequences, train 10 seq / 383 tracks / 27,882 boxes, test 2 seq / 119 tracks / 9,198 boxes (Tab. 3), 7 traffic classes, events 640x480, labels at 20 Hz, all moving (car-mounted) cameras, day/dusk/night; FE240hz single-object event dataset 346x260, up to 240 Hz, 4 selected test sequences. Only 2 test videos - very small. SMTrack: DanceTrack, BEE24, MOT17, MOT20 (standard splits, static or mild camera motion). SpikingMOT: DanceTrack, SportsMOT, SeaDroneSee (aerial, maritime), MOT17. FEMOTR: FEMOT 100 sequences (~200K frames, 14.58K trajectories, pedestrians and vehicles, DVS346 sensor, day and night, attributes incl. high exposure and similar appearance; split, resolution and frame rate not reported in the text read) plus DSEC-MOT. CSAM: COESOT, FE108, VisEvent (single-object RGB-event, attributes incl. low illumination LI and overexposure OE). Relation to BDD100K: only DSEC-MOT/FEMOT are driving-like with night scenes; none uses BDD100K; DSEC-MOT test set (2 videos) is far smaller than our val/train26 sets.

distinguishing_ablations: (a) SpikeMOT Tab. 7 is a backbone swap (CNN vs LSTM vs SNN of the same Siamese tracker), not 'base vs base + branch': the recurrent state accounts for most of the gain (CNN 46.2 -> LSTM 51.1 HOTA), spiking SRM adds +1.4 over LSTM; the equal-capacity non-spiking recurrent control (LSTM) is the right type of control and shows that the bio-inspired neuron itself adds little beyond recurrence; no seeds, 2 test videos, no CI. No ablation removes the detector/Hausdorff matcher to isolate the SNN identity contribution, and no appearance-ReID base exists. (b) SMTrack: no motion/identity ablation (spiking applies to detection); not relevant for an identity branch. (c) SpikingMOT Tab. 3a is a well-designed control set: sparsity-matched ANN alternatives (dropout, L1, top-k) of the same predictor give 72.9-73.6 vs 74.9 HOTA - a 'same capacity, non-spiking' control, but on SportsMOT only, single run; the predictor is motion-only and on MOT17 (appearance-ambiguous pedestrians) it is worse than appearance trackers (61.3 vs DeepSORT 63.8) - authors admit 'less benefit under prolonged occlusion and severe appearance ambiguity'. No appearance base, so no 'motion over strong appearance' evidence. (d) FEMOT Tab. 6 is the only MOT ablation 'appearance (RGB) vs appearance + event-motion modality' with the same architecture: +6.4 HOTA; but the event branch shares the backbone and is trained jointly, the RGB-only baseline is weak (23.7 HOTA for the baseline, suspicious gap to its fused 44.0), dataset contains night/high-exposure scenes where RGB fails - the gain is a sensor gain (new photons/HDR), not extra information from re-processing the same RGB pixels. (e) CSAM Tab. 3-4 is the closest to our question: frozen strong appearance base + learned matching with an event-motion embedding: whole matching network +2.6 SR; removing only the event-motion embedding costs -0.6 SR [uncertain mapping]; Tab. 4 shows the ENTIRE gain is in distractor sequences (S1 +0.0, S2 +5.1 SR) - direct evidence that an added motion cue over appearance is concentrated in the similar-neighbour regime and is zero elsewhere. Missing everywhere: an equal-capacity non-informative branch (permuted features), a no-bio motion control of the same role (box-velocity only) for the event branch, seeds and confidence intervals.
explanations_addressed: (1) Fly features carry no unique identity information beyond appearance: caution/design analogy - every positive 'motion over appearance' case here (FEMOT, CSAM) adds a NEW SENSOR (event camera, microsecond timing, HDR) rather than a re-processing of the same frames; SpikingMOT, the only RGB-only bio-inspired motion branch, uses box trajectories and does not beat appearance trackers on MOT17. FlyVis computes motion from the same grey pixels MASA sees, so by data-processing these sources give no reason to expect unique information beyond what box motion + appearance already hold; consistent with explanation (1). Not direct evidence. (2) Information exists but fusion ignores it (modality imbalance): not addressed; CSAM's two-stage scheme (freeze appearance, then train matching with motion) is an example of the 'unimodal pre-training then fusion' remedy and it produced a gain, but no ablation tests joint vs staged training. (3) Saved readout features lost the information: indirectly - SpikeMOT Fig. 9 shows longer temporal windows (voxel duration 30 -> 100 slices) help (51.1 -> 52.5 HOTA), i.e. the temporal integration window matters; our saved D/C features have a fixed short window over exemplar+search frames. Design analogy only. (4) FlyVis lacks a lobula/identity pathway: not addressed; none of the spiking trackers models object-selective cells; SpikeMOT gets identity from a learned template-matching Siamese head, i.e. an identity readout trained on same-vs-different pairs on top of a recurrent spiking front end - the functional role a lobula/LC readout would play. (5) Motion helps only in subsets diluted by averaging: DIRECT evidence from CSAM Tab. 4 (gain 0 on distractor-free sequences, +5.1 SR on distractor sequences); SpikingMOT text: benefit when 'complex dynamics dominate association errors'. Supports stratified evaluation. (6) Ceiling too low: not addressed; but the sizes of motion-branch gains over a strong appearance base here (+0.6 SR for the event-motion embedding in CSAM, +0.5..+0.9 HOTA for SpikingMOT over MambaTrack) are small, consistent with a small achievable share of our +2.8 pp ceiling.
evidence_strength: SpikeMOT: peer-reviewed (IEEE Access 2025), but only 2 test videos, single run, no CI, no code verified - weak. SMTrack: preprint plus IEEE IoT-J 2026 [uncertain], detector-only spiking, no identity ablation - weak for this question. SpikingMOT: preprint (Jul 2026), not independent of SMTrack (shared author, SMTrack as baseline), single runs, good sparsity-matched controls but no appearance base - weak-moderate for 'spiking motion predictor vs dense ANN', none for 'over appearance'. FEMOT: preprint (Jun 2026), suspicious weak RGB baseline, no variance - weak. CSAM: peer-reviewed NeurIPS 2024, frozen base, subset analysis with distractor split, three datasets; single runs, no CI, ablation row mapping reconstructed - moderate for 'motion embedding adds over frozen appearance only among distractors' but in SOT with an extra sensor. Overall: weak for any claim that a bio-inspired motion branch adds identity information over strong appearance in RGB MOT; no independent replication exists.
difference_from_tried: Already tried by us: frozen MASA cosines + snapped exemplar + 32 PCA products as base; FlyVis D/C/R1 saved regional features (incl. T4/T5) concatenated into gradient boosting; neighbour-relative features; T4/T5 motion consistency; tagged previous target; bank. Differences in these sources: (a) SpikeMOT trains the spiking front end END-TO-END on same/different-object template-search pairs with 25% same-category hard negatives - an identity-trained recurrent front end; we never trained the FlyVis core on identity (prepared, not run). (b) CSAM learns a per-candidate motion embedding and a transformer matching jointly over ALL candidates and over T=15 past frames with the appearance base frozen - set-level relational matching rather than per-region independent boosting; our boosting scores each region separately with neighbour means as features (partly similar), and has a 2-frame (exemplar+search) temporal context only. (c) SpikingMOT's per-tracklet prediction-error calibration of motion bases is a box-level recurrent state - functionally the same role as Kalman/ByteTrack prediction already in the bench; nothing new for identity. (d) FEMOT/CSAM gains come from an event sensor - unavailable on BDD100K (only frames), so not transferable at all. Net: the only untried mechanisms are (a) identity training of the recurrent front end and (b) long-horizon set-level matching; both already appear in our 'untried' list (core fine-tuning; learned projection).
math_precheck: CPU, saved features: runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/train26_features_{D,C,R1}.npz and the fit104 features behind runs/z13_hybrid_identity_v2_20261026. Step 1 (CSAM-style regime split, training-free): label each query as 'distractor' if MASA appearance is ambiguous - top-2 candidate cosine margin to the exemplar < 0.1 or >= 2 candidates of the same class overlapping the eye crop - else 'distractor-free'. Compute share of queries and share of the perfect-identity utility ceiling (+2.84 pp on train26) inside each stratum. Step 2 (where can a motion branch matter at most): with out-of-fold appearance-only predictions, oracle bound inside the distractor stratum = utility if appearance errors there were all corrected; if this bound is < 1.34 pp (the +2 pp criterion minus the measured appearance gain +0.66), no added branch confined to that stratum can reach the criterion -> STOP before GPU. Step 3 (unique information inside the stratum): paired comparison of out-of-fold log-loss of boosting on [MASA + box-motion] vs [MASA + box-motion + FlyVis D] restricted to distractor-stratum rows, with equal-size controls R1, stock C and within-query permuted D; video-level bootstrap CI of the log-loss gain (conditional V-information estimate). Step 4 (complementarity): fraction of appearance-wrong distractor queries where D-only top-1 is right vs where box-motion-only (Kalman distance + velocity-direction cosine) or R1-only top-1 is right. Step 5 (SpikeMOT/SpikingMOT lesson: recurrence vs bio neuron): if D does not beat R1 and a box-velocity control in Step 3/4, an identity-trained FlyVis core is unlikely to beat an equal-size LSTM/GRU on the same crops either (SpikeMOT: LSTM 51.1 vs SNN 52.5 HOTA; recurrence explained most of the gain). Decision rule: proceed to GPU core fine-tuning only if (i) the distractor-stratum oracle bound >= 1.34 pp, (ii) D's conditional log-loss gain over [MASA + box-motion] has a positive lower 95% CI bound and exceeds R1, C and permuted-D by a CI-separated margin, (iii) D is right on a larger share of appearance-wrong distractor queries than box-motion. Any failure = record 'no unique motion identity information in saved FlyVis features; node of failure = information content, not fusion' and do not train.
cue_role_and_regime: Roles in the sources: SpikeMOT - the spiking branch is the whole local identity tracker (template-search score map) validating position matches; SpikingMOT - motion predictor feeding IoU association (per-tracklet recurrent state); SMTrack - none (spiking detector); FEMOTR - early feature fusion of an extra modality; CSAM - per-candidate motion embedding inside learned matching among appearance-proposed distractors, base frozen. Regimes targeted: SpikeMOT - heavy occlusion, trajectory crossings, moving camera, low light in DSEC-MOT; SpikingMOT - non-linear fast motion and similar-looking players (DanceTrack, SportsMOT), explicitly weaker under severe appearance ambiguity (MOT17); FEMOT - night/high exposure/similar appearance; CSAM - distractors (similar candidates), low illumination and overexposure attributes, full occlusion. For our bench the transferable role is CSAM's: a per-candidate cue consulted inside the similar-neighbour stratum over a frozen MASA base; low-light/glare gains in FEMOT/CSAM come from event-sensor HDR and do not transfer to FlyVis on the same RGB frames.
no_fly_equivalent_control: (1) Box-trajectory motion of each candidate relative to the track: normalised centre distance to the ByteTrack/Kalman prediction, velocity-direction cosine (OC-SORT style), last-5-delta vector (SpikingMOT's input, H=5) - training-free, already derivable from tracker states. (2) A small GRU/LSTM over the same grey eye crops (exemplar + search frames) with parameter count matched to the FlyVis readout - the SpikeMOT Tab. 7 lesson: an equal-size non-bio recurrent network is the control that separates 'recurrence' from 'bio-inspired dynamics'. (3) A sparsity-matched non-spiking variant (SpikingMOT Tab. 3a: dropout / L1 / top-k) if a spiking or sparse FlyVis readout is proposed. (4) Eye input R1 (raw crop statistics) and stock FlyVis C under identical boosting. (5) Within-query permuted FlyVis rows (non-informative equal-capacity branch) - missing in all sources, required here. Three-way: MASA only / MASA + (1) or (2) / MASA + FlyVis D; FlyVis result only if the third beats the second.
bio_node_mapping: SpikeMOT: generic SRM spiking neurons (response + refractory kernels) on CNN synapses - no insect circuit; SpikingMOT: LIF gates + 'population coding' and 'predictive coding' analogies - no connectome; SMTrack: I-LIF neurons in a detector. None maps onto T4/T5, lobula LC/LPLC or STMD. FlyVis is the only connectome-constrained model in this comparison (T4/T5 and 34 output types; FlyWire 783 data in data/flywire/783 covers LC/LPLC inputs for a lobula-like extension). SpikingMOT's prediction-error calibration is functionally analogous to a recurrent prediction state (comparable role to FlyVis temporal state), but at box level, not retinotopic.
novelty_overlap: Nearest claims: SpikeMOT (spiking recurrent Siamese motion features for identity in event-based MOT on driving data) and CSAM (event-motion embedding added over a frozen appearance tracker to separate distractors); ours differs by using a connectome-constrained fly optic-lobe model on ordinary RGB frames as an added branch over frozen MASA appearance, with equal no-fly controls - no prior work found doing this.
candidate_node_change: Readout + training node (as implied by SpikeMOT/CSAM): train an identity readout of FlyVis activity on same-target vs same-class-neighbour pairs (SpikeMOT's 25% same-category hard negatives; CSAM's appearance-proposed distractors), with MASA frozen, applied only to candidates inside the similar-neighbour stratum; optionally fine-tune core parameters (connectome structure fixed) only if the readout stage passes. Why it addresses a FlyVis problem: FlyVis was trained for optic flow, not for discriminating one moving object from a similar neighbour; the sources obtain identity from motion only when the front end is trained on such pairs. Equal controls: MASA only; MASA + stock C; MASA + eye input R1; MASA + equal-size GRU on the same crops; MASA + box-motion (centre distance, velocity cosine, 5 deltas); MASA + permuted D. Condition to proceed to GPU: the CPU precheck (math_precheck Steps 1-4) passes - distractor-stratum oracle bound >= 1.34 pp and D's conditional gain over MASA + box-motion is CI-positive and exceeds R1/C/permuted-D; otherwise do not train.
strongest_objection: None of the sources shows a bio-inspired or spiking motion branch adding identity information over a strong appearance model on ordinary RGB frames: the spiking MOT papers either have no appearance base (SpikingMOT, SpikeMOT) or spike only in the detector (SMTrack), and the two positive 'motion over appearance' results (FEMOT, CSAM) owe their gain to an extra event sensor with HDR and microsecond timing that BDD100K lacks. Their own controls (SpikeMOT LSTM vs SNN; SpikingMOT sparsity-matched ANN) suggest the gain comes mostly from recurrence and training, not from bio-inspired neurons, which predicts that an equal-size GRU on the same crops would match an identity-trained FlyVis. All evidence is single-run, on small or non-driving test sets (DSEC-MOT test = 2 videos).
cost_and_hardware: CPU precheck on saved train26/fit104 features: minutes of compute, a few hours of analysis (box-motion controls from saved tracker states; equal-size GRU control on saved crops would need crops re-extraction [uncertain: whether eye crops are stored]). Identity-trained FlyVis readout/core (SpikeMOT-style pair training) needs new FlyVis activity and the single 12 GB GPU - justified only if the decision rule passes. Event-sensor mechanisms (FEMOT, CSAM) are not reproducible on BDD100K.
